subject: Maths
title: Frequency tables and grouped data
subtitle: Statistics · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate averages and other statistics from frequency tables and grouped frequency tables.

key_vocab.definition: A frequency table shows how often each value (or group of values) occurs. For grouped data, use the midpoint of each class to estimate the mean.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate averages and other statistics from frequency tables and grouped frequency tables.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: frequency table -- A frequency table shows how often each value (or group of values) occurs. For grouped data, use the midpoint of each class to estimate the mean.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
For grouped data: estimate mean = sum of (frequency × midpoint) divided by total frequency.
Estimated mean = Σfx ÷ Σf
x = midpoint of each class; f = frequency

Key examples:
  ✓ Mean = Σfx ÷ Σf  (total of fx divided by total frequency)
  ✓ Midpoint of 10–20 is 15  ((10 + 20) ÷ 2)
  ✓ Modal class = class with highest frequency  (not the midpoint)
  ✗ Mean of grouped data uses class boundaries  (use midpoints)
  ✗ You can find the exact mean from grouped data  (only an estimate)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – ungrouped frequency table
  Scores: 1(f=3), 2(f=5), 3(f=7), 4(f=4), 5(f=1). Find the mean.
  Σfx = 1×3 + 2×5 + 3×7 + 4×4 + 5×1 = 3+10+21+16+5 = 55
  Σf = 3+5+7+4+1 = 20
  Mean = 55 ÷ 20 = 2.75
  Mean = 2.75
  (Multiply each value by its frequency, sum, then divide by total frequency.)

Example 2 – grouped data mean
  Heights (cm): 140–150 (f=4), 150–160 (f=10), 160–170 (f=8), 170–180 (f=3). Estimate the mean.
  Midpoints: 145, 155, 165, 175
  Σfx = 145×4 + 155×10 + 165×8 + 175×3 = 580+1550+1320+525 = 3975
  Mean = 3975 ÷ 25 = 159
  Estimated mean = 159 cm
  (Use midpoints because we do not know exact values within groups.)

sections.title: Mixed frequency table problems
sections.content:
Answer each question.

(a) n=30, Σfx = 450. Find the mean.
(b) Mean = 8, n = 25. Find Σfx.
(c) Classes: 0–20(f=8), 20–40(f=12), 40–60(f=5). Range estimate?
(d) Modal class for: 1–3(f=4), 3–5(f=9), 5–7(f=6), 7–9(f=1)?
(e) Estimated mean if all in class 10–20 are exactly 15?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Mean from a frequency table = Σfx ÷ Σf
✗ For grouped data, use the class boundaries (not midpoints) for the mean
✓ The modal class is the class with the highest frequency
✗ You can find the exact mean from grouped data
✓ The midpoint of a class 10–20 is 15

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Mean from ungrouped frequency tables:
  (a) Mean = (5+16+12+12)/20 = 45/20 = 2.25
  (b) Mean = (0+6+18+21+4)/25 = 49/25 = 1.96
  (c) Mean = (20+60+56+24)/25 = 160/25 = 6.4
  (d) Mean = (70+100+240)/20 = 410/20 = 20.5

Estimated mean (grouped):
  (a) Mean = (30+150+100)/20 = 280/20 = 14
  (b) Mean = (7.5+60+112.5)/20 = 180/20 = 9
  (c) Midpoints: 55,65,75,85; mean = (275+780+600+425)/30 = 2080/30 = 69.3
  (d) Mean = (440+910+1350)/20 = 2700/20 = 135

Modal class and median class:
  (a) Modal: 10–20; Median in 10–20
  (b) Modal: 5–10; Median in 5–10
  (c) Modal: 30–40; Median in 30–40
  (d) Modal: 100–200; Median in 100–200

Median and mode from ungrouped:
  (a) Mode=3; n=20, median at 10/11th, CF: 2,7,15... median=3
  (b) Mode=1 and 2 (bimodal); n=20, median between 10th/11th = 1.5
  (c) Mode=12; n=20, median at 10/11th = 12
  (d) Mode=4; n=20, median at 10/11th = 4

Mixed frequency table problems:
  (a) 15
  (b) 200
  (c) 60
  (d) 3–5
  (e) That is the midpoint assumption
